category_title: Students with disabilities who do not respond to teacher questions or volunteer for individual performances
minimal_context: Adam is participating in a dyad talking activity with a partner in his inclusive music classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Okay everyone, it is time for our dyad talking activity, so please turn to your partner and discuss the music.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly and looks away from his partner, not participating in the dyad talking activity.)

TUTOR: Adam, you should be talking with your partner now.

STUDENT: (Remains silent and looks around the classroom, staying off-task during the activity.)

TUTOR: What do you think? Go ahead and share.

STUDENT: (Continues to be completely off-task, not responding or engaging in the dyad talking activity at all.)

options.A: Develop a series of real-life social stories that explicitly describe the beneficial course of action.
options.B: Ask follow-up questions to model conversational skills for the student during the dyad talking activity.
options.C: Establish, through consensus, the working practices of the dyad via a pledge and reinforce it.
options.D: Maximize the time the student is engaged in active music-making experiences during the session.
